subject: Clarifications on MSA/order form: model use and training carve-outs
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@bluepeak.ai>

Cc: BluePeak Contracts <contracts@bluepeak.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on MSA / Order Form - model output & training

Hi Alex,

Thanks for sending the revised Order Form. Our legal team flagged a couple of items they need to be crystal-clear on before we proceed:

1) Output ownership: the order form currently references 'customer content' and an output license to the customer, but the MSA has broader language on feedback/training. We need confirmation that BluePeak will have exclusive ownership of generated outputs for our use-cases (customer-facing analytics), and any Redwood use of outputs for model training would require opt-in + compensation.

2) Training/Feedback license: the MSA's current feedback clause grants Redwood a perpetual license to use any feedback data for model improvement. For regulated datasets, we need either (a) a carve-out for data used in model training, or (b) an explicit process (and notice) before Redwood ingests any data for training.

Can you share Redwood's preferred clause language or any proposed redlines? We attached the Order Form v5 with our markups.

Appreciate a quick run-through — our procurement window is tight.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships
BluePeak Analytics

Maya — thanks for the clear note and the markup. Looping in Laura from Legal and Karthik for the technical implications. High-level response:

- We are comfortable granting customers a broad, perpetual right to use and commercialize generated outputs for their business operations; we typically do not claim ownership over customer outputs.
- On training/feedback, Redwood's standard approach is to request a limited feedback license to improve models, but we can carve out regulated or sensitive data and require explicit opt-in. There are a couple of ways to handle this in contract language (see Laura's proposed edit coming shortly).

Immediate asks:
- Laura: can you propose concrete language for (A) output attribution/ownership and (B) a training/feedback carve-out and notice flow?
- Karthik: can you summarize what data types we consider RISKY for training and how the opt-in workflow would look operationally?

I'll hold off on redlines until we have Laura's text so we don't create divergent drafts.

Thanks — Alex

Alex / Laura / Maya — quick technical note from infra/ops:

- Data types that we classify as sensitive for training: PII that cannot be pseudonymized reliably (SSNs, full credit card numbers), PHI as defined under HIPAA, and datasets subject to customer confidentiality clauses or export controls.
- For customers that opt-in, ingestion for training would be through a controlled pipeline: data marking -> staging in encrypted buckets -> auditors notified -> training dataset flagged as "customer-consented".
- Opt-in toggle: we can implement a per-tenant flag in our private settings or an API call that flags data as eligible/non-eligible. Implementation lead-time: ~3 weeks to add audit hooks + UI for consent tracking; we can do a contractual interim where Redwood agrees to not use any customer data for training without express, documented consent.

Happy to provide an operations note for Laura to include as an exhibit if helpful.

— Karthik
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on MSA / Order Form - model output & training

Maya / team — thanks. I've drafted concise contract language below that should address BluePeak's concerns while keeping Redwood's ability to improve models where permitted. I'm attaching a tracked changes doc (Redwood-Proposed-IP-Amendment_v3.docx) and an annotated Order Form.

Proposed clauses (high level):

1) Customer Outputs.
"Customer Outputs" means the outputs generated by the Licensed Model in response to Customer Input. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, transferable right to use, reproduce, distribute, and create derivative works of Customer Outputs for Customer's internal and commercial purposes. Redwood expressly disclaims ownership of Customer Outputs.

2) Feedback and Training Carve-out.
Subject to the Customer's instructions and any data handling settings in the Order Form, Redwood shall not use Customer Input, Customer Outputs, or metadata that contains "Regulated Data" to improve or retrain Redwood's models for general improvement unless Customer provides an explicit, documented opt-in. "Regulated Data" includes PHI, government-identifying numbers, and any data that Customer designates as Confidential in writing. If Customer opts-in, Redwood will: (a) process such data through the agreed consent pipeline; (b) notify Customer of the intended use and duration; and (c) provide an option to revoke consent, after which Redwood shall cease inclusion of subsequently gathered data from the Customer in model training.

3) Auditability and Controls.
Redwood will maintain an audit log of data marked for training, accessible to authorized Customer reviewers under reasonable confidentiality terms, and will provide a quarterly summary of training datasets derived from Customer opt-ins.

Practical notes: the opt-in can be surfaceable in the Order Form as a checkbox + API flag. Karthik's implementation notes line up with our security requirements. If BluePeak needs stronger guarantees (e.g., HSM attestations, or encryption-at-rest key segregation), we can add those to the Order Form as paid options.

Next steps:
- Maya / Contracts: review the attached tracked changes, and let us know which of the three options you prefer (full opt-out for training, opt-in with audit logs, or negotiated paid isolation).
- Alex / Karthik: if we move the opt-in into the Order Form, I'll prepare the exact wording for the checkbox/API snippet and a short exhibit describing the consent flow.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks, this is very helpful and much closer to what our legal team needs. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

- Can you make the opt-in process explicit in the Order Form (checkbox text + short definition) rather than buried in an exhibit? We want the default to be "no training" unless checked.
- The audit log access will need an SLA for response times when we request evidence. Would Redwood include a 10-business-day response target for ad-hoc audit requests?
- For the definition of Regulated Data, can we add "data subject to data residency or export-control obligations"?

Assuming we get those small edits, we can move to redlines and run this through procurement next week. I'll have our contracts team upload a redline by EOD Monday.
